claims.statement: Dynamic contracts available to eligible Polish households and micro-enterprises calculate energy prices at intervals tied to short-term markets, creating a measurable timing exposure on electricity consumption.
Eligible households and micro-enterprises already own the electricity bill affected by dynamic pricing, but their willingness to pay for independent optimization is not established.
A plausible control path is direct household authorization plus replaceable vendor integrations, beginning with a read-only planner; no authorization or integration agreement has been obtained.
URE reported only 135 dynamic-price customers in the first measured period, which is evidence of very early adoption rather than mass demand.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Property owner or small-business owner responsible for the electricity bill
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Cross-brand orchestration, transparent realized-savings measurement, and installer-neutral recommendations must outperform free single-vendor controls
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Electricity retailers own the supply relationship; the proposed optimization relationship has no current owner
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Installer handoff at commissioning, followed by referral and prosumer-community acquisition

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Installer commissions plus content/community acquisition; actual CAC is unknown
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Monthly or annual prepayment; integration development and support occur before scale
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Potentially software-like after integrations stabilize, but unproven and reduced materially by support-heavy device fragmentation
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Compatibility onboarding, exception handling, safety constraints, and household support
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Security, GDPR, product liability review, device-testing bench, accounting, and insurance
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Target 29-59 PLN per site per month, with an optional installer revenue share
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Weather and price feeds, device-cloud calls, notifications, payment fees, and installer referral share

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Utilities and device makers can bundle basic scheduling into supply contracts or proprietary apps
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Subscription activation is the paid event; avoidable loss is the spread between unmanaged and constraint-aware consumption or export under time-varying prices
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Enrollment in a dynamic tariff, commissioning of flexible electrical equipment, or an unexpectedly poor first bill
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Monthly renewal after a savings and comfort report

contrary_evidence: URE reported just 135 dynamic-price customers in the initial measured period, so the addressable early-adopter pool may be tiny.
Utilities are free to shape dynamic offers with caps, exclusions, or commercial fees, which can reduce dispatchable savings.
PV net-billing RCE and retail dynamic-tariff formulas are not necessarily the same price signal.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed customer authorization plus vendor API or local-gateway terms; no agreement is secured
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Launch with price alerts and read-only schedules using user-entered device constraints, then support replaceable local relays where lawful and safe
critical_control_point.current_owner: The household and its chosen electricity and device vendors
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Electricity retailers own the supply relationship; the proposed optimization relationship has no current owner
critical_control_point.duration: Unknown until customer and integration terms are executed
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The family renewable-energy installer can lawfully introduce a small opt-in test set, but no customer, device, or supplier access is presently contracted
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Each opt-in household together with relevant integration providers
critical_control_point.renewal: Proposed monthly customer renewal; integration renewal is unknown
critical_control_point.subject: Household device-dispatch workflow and its authorized data connections

economics.acquisition_route: Installer-introduced pilots, prosumer groups, and bill-analysis lead magnets
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Conditional path: 8,000 sites at 45 PLN monthly equals 4.32m PLN ARR; a profitable multi-market software asset could support a value above 5m PLN, but adoption and margin are wholly unvalidated
economics.founder_time: Read-only MVP and 10-20 pilots can fit roughly 3-5 hours daily; full device control requires later engineering and support capacity
economics.gross_margin_basis: Software revenue less data/API, payments, support, and channel share; no realized margin evidence yet
economics.payback: Target customer payback under four months from verified savings; currently unknown
economics.pricing: Discovery hypothesis: 29-59 PLN per site monthly or 299-599 PLN annually; validate against verified net savings
economics.retention_or_repeat: Monthly use tied to recurring bills, with churn risk if tariffs flatten or automation disappoints

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Consent-based device-response and realized-savings data improve forecasts, compatibility coverage, and household-specific scheduling
fingerprint.customer: Polish prosumer households and micro-enterprises with remotely read meters plus at least one flexible load
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Referral distribution through independent renewable-energy installers, energy-efficiency advisers, and targeted prosumer communities
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Cross-vendor energy dispatch software sold as a monthly subscription, initially read-only recommendations and later opt-in control
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The household or micro-enterprise pays a recurring subscription when automated scheduling is activated for a site
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Signing a dynamic-price contract or adding PV, a home battery, heat pump, or EV charger creates repeated decisions about when to consume, store, or export electricity

founder_fit: Time-series forecasting and optimization match the founder's data-science background
A lawful installer relationship offers bounded customer discovery and pilot introductions without employer resources
A read-only MVP can be built alongside employment within the five-hours-per-day constraint
The model is measurable and can become increasingly automated rather than requiring on-camera selling
risks: Unsafe or incorrect dispatch could damage equipment or household trust
Device vendors can close interfaces or copy the scheduling feature
Savings claims could become misleading without counterfactual measurement
Support burden across fragmented devices can erase subscription margin

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: per site household energy optimization subscription
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: constraint aware dispatch layer across tariff and household devices
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: heterogeneous meter and device interfaces with sufficiently reliable data or control

structure.control_point: The recurring household workflow that converts tariff and device data into a dispatch schedule
structure.critical_dependency: Reliable access to meter, tariff, inverter, battery, charger, and heat-pump data or control interfaces

thesis: Observed transaction change: large Polish electricity retailers must offer dynamic-price contracts, exposing eligible households and micro-enterprises with remotely read meters to short-interval prices, while reported uptake began at only 135 customers. Sell an independent, cross-brand scheduler that turns tomorrow's prices, household constraints, PV, batteries, heat pumps, and EV charging into an auditable dispatch plan rather than asking users to watch prices manually.
title: Household Flex Dispatcher for Polish Dynamic Tariffs
uncertainties: Share of Polish sites with both remote meters and controllable flexible loads
Actual API access, latency, warranty impact, and safe-control constraints by device brand
Savings after taxes, distribution charges, comfort constraints, battery degradation, and retailer-specific formulas
Household willingness to pay before dynamic tariffs become mainstream
